format.label: Formatting
format.description: Whitespace, indentation, line wrapping, and import ordering

lint.label: Linting
lint.description: Static analysis for likely bugs and bad patterns

code-quality.label: Code Quality
code-quality.description: Complexity limits, dead code detection, and duplication checks

ai-slop.label: AI Slop
ai-slop.description: Narrative comments, dead patterns, unsafe type casts, TODO stubs, generic names

security.label: Security
security.description: Secret leaks, risky APIs, and dependency vulnerabilities

diagnostics.message: Unused code check skipped: Knip is not set up in this project
diagnostics.help: Unused files, exports and dependencies were not checked. Add a knip config file (for example knip.json) or add knip to devDependencies to enable the check, or set quality.knip: always to run it without that setup.

scoreImpact.rationale: A skipped unused code check is visibility loss, not evidence of dead code.

diagnostics.message: `print()` in production code — usually a leftover debug statement.
diagnostics.help: Use the project's logger (`logging.getLogger(__name__).info(...)`). If this file is genuinely a CLI entry point (typer/click/argparse), it's safe to ignore — but rename to `__main__.py` or move under `scripts/` so the rule skips it next time.

scoreImpact.rationale: Debug print output is cleanup unless it leaks sensitive data.

diagnostics.message: 5 repeated branches dispatch on `kind`.
diagnostics.help: Use a table, set membership, or handler map when branches share the same shape. SlopCodeBench highlights these selector ladders as code that keeps growing instead of absorbing new cases cleanly.

scoreImpact.rationale: Repetitive dispatch ladders create maintainability debt.

diagnostics.message: Imports "reportlab" but it's not declared in requirements files, pyproject.toml, or Pipfile and isn't Python stdlib
diagnostics.help: Most often this is an LLM hallucinating a plausible-sounding package name. Either add the package to your manifest, or correct the import. If your runtime provides it, list it under imports.provided in .aislop/config.yml.

scoreImpact.rationale: Imports missing from the manifest are high-confidence install/runtime failures.
